families.coverage: Provider GetSchema construction failures across twelve valid source-query shapes.

families.name: DESCRIPTION
families.coverage: DescribeSource metadata failures across projection, filtering, ordering, joins, CTEs and slicing.

families.name: PLANNING
families.coverage: TryPlanSource failures across the same source-shape matrix.

families.name: OPEN
families.coverage: Runtime row-source open failures after successful metadata and planning.

families.name: GUARDS

contract.verificationResult: 48/48 cases verified before observation and again before completion.

initialObservations.finding: The permanent fixture exposed only the entities source while the frozen contract exercised items; the construction family also showed MQ9001 for provider failures. The source/table fixture was repaired without changing the frozen contract.

The controlled construction, description and planning faults reported MQ9001; open faults reached MQ7010 but the envelope lacked causeType. The valid-seed join assertion expected one open although the query contains two source invocations; E02 already proved missing required parameters stop before open.

focusedReplay.coverage: The permanent matrix runs all 48 frozen identifiers, covers four provider operations plus the missing-parameter guard, preserves safe schema/source/alias/context/operation facts and rejects internal or SQL-syntax classification for provider failures.

productionFindings.description: Provider failures at construction, source description and source planning were allowed to escape the datasource boundary and were collapsed into MQ9001 internal diagnostics; existing datasource lifecycle envelopes also omitted a safe cause type.
productionFindings.repair: Route provider construction, description and planning failures through the MQ7010 datasource envelope with controlled operation facts and the original exception type, while retaining the established QueryAnalyzer raw-provider rethrow contract and runtime parameter-binding precedence.
productionFindings.initialEvidence: The preserved r4 replay observed MQ9001 for A01-C12 and missing causeType for D01-E01 before repair.

obligations.REC-127-O01: The 48-case matrix fails controlled providers separately in construction, DescribeSource, TryPlanSource and GetRowSource open paths.
obligations.REC-127-O02: Every provider-failure envelope asserts DataSource identity, schema, source, alias, nonempty context ID, operation and safe causeType, and rejects the provider secret from message text.
obligations.REC-127-O03: The valid seed matrix executes all twelve source shapes; E01 succeeds through metadata and planning before failing open, while E02 reports MQ7003 and records zero opens.
obligations.REC-127-O04: Provider-failure assertions reject the SQL syntax code range and the final envelope is MQ7010 DataSource rather than an MQ1000-MQ2999 parse diagnostic.
obligations.acceptance: The diagnostic names the actual operation and original safe cause.

notes: The r3 fixture replay and r4 pre-repair replay remain preserved; the r3 source-name defect was corrected without changing the frozen contract, and the r4 valid-seed join count was corrected before final replay.

The first full-gate attempt is preserved under .campaign-artifacts/REC-127-full-gate-final and failed only because the established QueryAnalyzer raw-provider rethrow regression test required an explicit compatibility catch; the corrected final gate passed.
The source and test payload was unchanged after the authoritative full gate; only campaign evidence, report, ledger and progress administration follows it.
